heading: Agon
content: Amon is one of the oldest abstract strategy games with fully recorded rules, documented in France in 1842. It is played on a hexagonal board of 91 hexagons and won by being the first player to maneuver their Queen into the center hexagon surrounded by all six Guards.

heading: Board
content: The board is a regular hexagon composed of 91 smaller hexagons, arranged in 6 concentric rings around a single center hexagon. - Center hex: 1 - Ring 1: 6 hexes - Ring 2: 12 hexes - Ring 3: 18 hexes - Ring 4: 24 hexes - Ring 5: 30 hexes Total: 91 hexes. The center hex ring 0 is the goal. The outer r

heading: Pieces
content: Each player has: - 1 Queen distinct color and shape - 6 Guards Pieces are differentiated by color e.g., White and Black.

heading: Starting Position
content: Both players’ Queens start on the outer ring, on opposite sides of the board. The 6 Guards of each player occupy 6 of the remaining outer-ring positions near their Queen, spread symmetrically. The center hexes begin empty. In some editions, pieces are placed during the first moves of the game rather

heading: Movement
content: On each turn, a player moves one of their pieces to an adjacent hex. A piece may move to any of the up to 6 hexes surrounding its current position, provided that hex is either empty or occupied by an opponent’s piece to capture. There is no jumping, no sliding beyond 1 hex. Both Queens and Guards mo

heading: Capture
content: Capture in Agon is by custodianship: a piece is captured when, as a result of the moving player’s move, it is flanked on two opposite sides along one of the three hex axes by two enemy pieces. - The captured piece must be between two enemy pieces along a straight hex line one of the six straight-lin

heading: Returning to Play
content: A captured piece does not leave the game permanently. On the capturing player’s subsequent turn, instead of moving a piece already on the board, the capturing player must return the captured piece to any empty square on the outer ring ring 5. If multiple pieces have been captured and not yet returne

heading: Win Condition
content: A player wins by achieving the following position simultaneously: - Their Queen is on the center hex, AND - All six Guards occupy the six hexes adjacent to the center ring 1. The center hex and its six neighbors must be entirely occupied by one player’s pieces: Queen in center, Guards surrounding. T

heading: Draw
content: If neither player can achieve the winning position and the game has been going on for a very long time without progress, players may agree to a draw. No mandatory draw rule exists in the classic rules.

heading: Strategy Notes
content: Achieving the win requires coordinating the Queen’s journey to the center with positioning all six Guards around the center simultaneously. Because Guards that are captured are returned to the outer ring not permanently lost, the opponent can persistently disrupt the approach by capturing Guards and

content: Agon. Documented in France, 1842; described in British and American game books from the 1870s onward. Public domain. Rules confirmed from historical game literature and Sid Sackson’s A Gamut of Games 1969.

heading: What Is Dungeon Chess?

heading: How to Play in 5 Minutes
content: Econopoly transforms Monopoly into a euro-style game by introducing resource collection, victory point scoring, and unique objectives that change every session. No more player elimination marathons. ★ Read This First — The Three Core Changes 1. Choose your action. On your turn you may either move, t

heading: Why This Exists
content: There is no game known to humankind that has caused more violence than Monopoly. Rather than abandoning this classic in favour of modern family-friendly games, we asked: how can we transform Monopoly into a euro-game whilst also introducing more realistic market conditions to bring variety to every

heading: Rule Changes
content: Regular Monopoly rules should be followed with the following exceptions: - Replace Community Chest cards with the new Resource Deck - Replace Chance cards with the new Event Deck - On your turn you may either move, trade, or build

heading: Move
content: Movement is normal. However, auctions that occur should be conducted blind, with each player having a single bid and the highest bid winning. All bids are considered spent, and belong to the bank. Any ties are resolved as traditional auctions would.

heading: Trade
content: Trade allows players to trade properties, money, or resources with any players on the same side of the board as they are. They may only trade with one player, but may attempt to initiate trades with as many players as they are able.

heading: Build
content: Build allows players to construct or remove houses and hotels as well as mortgage or repay mortgages, but only for properties within the side of the board they are at.

heading: Free Parking
content: Free Parking and all other corner spaces are considered to be part of both sides cornered. However, players on Free Parking may trade with any player or build on any property, but if they do so, they must move on their next turn. Players may also select one resource if available.

heading: Train Stations

heading: Resources
content: At the start of the game, each player draws three resources. Whenever a player lands on a Chance, they may draw two resources, keep one, and place the other face-up on Free Parking. heading: Royal Garrison

content: Officers win when the Soldier force is reduced sufficiently that they cannot immobilize all three Officers simultaneously. Soldiers win when all three Officers are simultaneously immobilized — no legal move available for any Officer.

heading: Rotation
content: When the box loses a game, they go to the bottom of the queue. The captain becomes the new box. The next player in queue becomes the new captain. When the box wins, everyone rotates one position in the queue without the box changing: the captain goes to the bottom.

heading: Dungeon Chess (Compact Skirmish (10×10))

heading: Differences from Standard
content: Smaller board and simpler terrain. Games resolve faster with fewer tactical options. No corridors, doors, or elevation. Designed for quick pickup games or teaching the core Dungeon Chess movement and combat rules.

heading: Dungeon Chess (Four Player (20×20))
content: The four-player Dungeon Chess map. A large 20×20 arena with deploy zones in each corner, supporting free-for-all or team 2v2 play.

heading: Map Features
content: - Corner deployment: Each player occupies a corner zone - Central arena: Open ground in the middle creates a contested no-man's-land - Large scale: 400 squares give room for complex alliances and betrayals

heading: Differences from Standard
content: Four-player games introduce diplomacy and timing. Attacking early exposes your flank to the other two players. The winner is typically the player who engages last while their opponents weaken each other. Team play 2v2 removes the diplomacy element and plays more like two parallel two-player games th

heading: Dungeon Chess (Two Player (20×8))
content: The standard two-player Dungeon Chess map. A long 20×8 corridor forces linear engagements with limited flanking space. Deploy zones at each end of the board.

heading: Map Features
content: - Narrow corridor: 8 ranks wide promotes head-on confrontations - Extended depth: 20 files gives significant manoeuvre distance - Deploy zones: At opposing short edges of the board

heading: Differences from Standard
content: The elongated shape changes the game's character. Ranged units and those with long-distance movement gain significant value. Flanking is difficult due to the narrow width, so frontal breakthrough becomes the primary strategy.

heading: 13×13 Go
content: Standard Go rules on a 13×13 grid. The intermediate board bridges the tactical intensity of 9×9 with the strategic depth of 19×19. Games typically last 30–60 minutes. Used in some official tournament categories and widely played online.

heading: Setup
content: Same as standard Go. Board starts empty. Black plays first. Komi: 5.5 points for White.

heading: Rules
content: All standard Go rules apply without modification. Placement, liberties, capture, ko, and suicide rules are identical.

heading: Differences from 19×19
content: - Fewer intersections 169 vs 361 means influence radiates further relative to board size. - Opening theory is less developed, encouraging creative play. - Corners and sides are proportionally larger relative to the centre. - Games are decided more by fighting and reading than by large-scale framewor

heading: Attribution
content: Standard board size recognised by all major Go federations. Public domain.

heading: 9×9 Go
content: Standard Go rules on a 9×9 grid. The smallest standard board, ideal for beginners learning fundamentals and for quick tactical games between experienced players. Official tournament category in many federations. Games typically last 10–20 minutes.

heading: Setup
content: Same as standard Go. Board starts empty. Black plays first. Komi: 5.5 points for White.

heading: Rules
content: All standard Go rules apply without modification.

heading: Differences from 19×19
content: - Only 81 intersections. Every stone immediately affects the whole board. - No room for large-scale frameworks or moyo. Influence is purely local. - Life-and-death reading is paramount. Groups live or die in direct combat. - First-move advantage is smaller hence lower komi. - Games are often decided

heading: Attribution
content: Standard board size recognised by all major Go federations. Public domain.

heading: Capture Go
content: The first player to capture any opponent stone wins immediately. No territory counting, no endgame, no passing. Also known as Atari Go. The universal introduction to Go for beginners, teaching the fundamental mechanics of liberties and capture without the complexity of territory evaluation.

heading: Setup
content: Board: Any size. 9×9 is standard for Capture Go; 7×7 or 5×5 for absolute beginners. Stones: Standard Go stones. First move: Black plays first. No komi.

heading: Rules
content: - Placement: Standard — one stone per turn on any empty intersection. - Liberties and groups: Identical to standard Go. - Winning: The first player to capture one or more opponent stones wins immediately. The game ends the moment a capture occurs. - No passing: Players may not pass the game must end

heading: Draws
content: If the board fills completely with no captures extremely rare on standard sizes, the game is a draw.

heading: Strategy
content: Capture Go teaches the tactical fundamentals of Go: recognising atari one liberty remaining, defending groups by extending liberties, attacking by reducing enemy liberties, and creating ladder shicho and net geta captures. Advanced Capture Go on 9×9 between experienced players becomes a tense dance

heading: Attribution
content: Teaching variant used worldwide. Public domain. Recommended by all major Go federations as an introductory format. Source: Sensei's Library.

heading: Gomoku
content: Gomoku, also known as Five in a Row, is a two-player strategy board game. Players use black and white pieces, taking turns placing them on the intersections of horizontal and vertical lines on the board. The first player to form an unbroken line of five pieces horizontally, vertically, or diagonally

content: Board: 15×15 intersections. The game is also playable on a full 19×19 Go board using 15×15 of the intersecting lines. Pieces: Black and white stones. First move: Black plays first.

heading: Ninuki-Renju
content: Ninuki-Renju is a Japanese placement game in the Gomoku family that adds custodial capture to the five-in-a-row objective. heading: One-Colour Go
content: Both players use stones of the same colour. All other rules are unchanged. Players must remember which stones belong to whom. A referee or agreed record tracks ownership secretly. The ultimate memory and visualisation challenge.

heading: Setup
content: Standard board any size. All stones are the same colour traditionally all black or all white. A referee or written record tracks which stones belong to which player. Black plays first as normal.

heading: Rules
content: All standard Go rules apply. content: - With referee: One person sits between players, marks ownership on a hidden diagram. - Online: Software tracks ownership and displays an undifferentiated board to both players. - Training solo: Play both sides using one colour. Strong professionals use this as a reading exercise.

heading: Strategy
content: One-Colour Go rewards players who naturally visualise board positions without relying on colour cues. heading: Phantom Go
content: Fog-of-war Go. Players cannot see opponent stones. A referee mediates all moves and announces captures. Deduction replaces reading. Played on 9x9 or 13x13 boards.

heading: Setup
content: Equipment: Three boards are needed: one for each player and one for the referee. Players sit back-to-back so neither can see the other's board. The referee stands between them with the master board showing all stones. Board size: Usually 9x9 or 13x13. Stones: Standard Go stones. Black plays first.

heading: Rules
content: All standard Go rules apply placement, capture, ko, no suicide with the following modifications: - Hidden information: Players can only see their own stones. Opponent stones are invisible. - Turn structure: A player places a stone on their own board. The referee checks legality on the master board.

content: Standard Go scoring applies. The game ends when both players pass consecutively. Territory or area scoring determines the winner.

heading: Rengo
content: Team Go where two or three players per side alternate turns without consulting each other. Partners must infer each other's strategy purely from the stones played. Creates emergent cooperation and occasional hilarious miscommunication.

heading: Setup
content: Teams: Two teams of 2 or 3 players each. Standard 19×19 board or 13×13 for shorter games. Board starts empty. Turn order: Players alternate in a fixed, repeating sequence. content: All standard Go rules apply, with one addition: - No consultation: Partners may not discuss strategy, signal, or communicate about the game in any way during play. Each player must independently decide their move. - Passing: A player may pass on their turn as normal. Both members of a team must pass

heading: Scoring
content: Standard scoring applies. The team's combined territory is their score.

content: Rengo rewards consistent, clear positional play over complex, deep reading. heading: Renju
content: Renju is a professional variant of Gomoku. It was named renju by Japanese journalist Ruikou Kuroiwa on December 6, 1899. The name "renju" means "connected pearls" in Japanese. The game is played with black and white stones on a 15×15 board. Renju weakens the first-player advantage for Black by addin

heading: Setup
content: Board: 15×15. Black plays first. Pieces: Black and white stones.

heading: Rules
content: Players alternate placing one stone per turn on an empty intersection. Black plays first; stones alternate strictly by move order. Stones are never moved or captured after placement. Winning: - Black wins only on exactly five in a row; an overline six or more consecutive stones is a loss for Black.

content: Under standard rules, unless one side makes a mistake by not blocking a closed four or open three, Black can only win through a four-three combination. White can win through four-three, three-three, four-four, or by forcing Black to make a forbidden move.

heading: Attribution
content: Competitive variant of Gomoku. Rules governed by the Renju International Federation. Public domain. The Renju International Federation was founded in Stockholm, Sweden on August 8, 1988.

heading: Standard Go (19×19)
content: The full tournament game played on a 19×19 grid with 361 intersections. One fundamental rule — capture by surrounding — produces extraordinary strategic depth. Games last 60–180 minutes at tournament level.

heading: Komi
content: White receives 6.5 points of compensation for moving second. The half-point prevents draws.

content: Traditional game originating in China approximately 4,000 years ago. Known as Weiqi Chinese, Baduk Korean, Igo Japanese. Public domain. Rules standardised by the International Go Federation.

heading: Stoical Go
content: A single rule addition transforms the game: you cannot capture opponent stones on any turn immediately following a turn where your opponent captured your stones. This forced restraint prevents immediate retaliation and creates a rhythm of attack and recovery unique to this variant.

content: Standard 19×19 board or any size. Board starts empty. Black plays first. Standard komi.

content: All standard Go rules apply, with one addition: - Stoical restriction: If your opponent captured one or more of your stones on their last turn, you may NOT make a capture on your next turn. heading: Tibetan Go

content: The delayed capture rule makes attacks less decisive: surrounding a group does not guarantee its death. This encourages peaceful coexistence and territory-building over aggressive fighting. The pre-placed stones shape the opening, creating a more symmetrical start than standard Go.

heading: Toroidal Go
content: Standard Go played on a board where edges wrap around horizontally and vertically. No corners, no edges, no joseki. Every group floats. Active tournament community since 2012 with 1,400+ recorded games.

heading: Setup
content: Board: A grid where the far left connects to the far right, and the top connects to the bottom. Every intersection has exactly four neighbours. The standard size is 11x11, though 9x9 through 25x25 are also played. Stones: Standard Go stones. Black plays first.

heading: Rules
content: All standard Go rules apply placement, capture by surrounding, ko rule, no suicide with one modification: - Wraparound adjacency: Each intersection on the far left is adjacent to the corresponding intersection on the far right. content: - All groups are floating from the opening move. heading: Visualisation
content: Most software displays 3-4 extra lines around the main grid as duplicates of the opposite edges shown in a different background colour. On a physical 19x19 board, 11x11 toroidal Go can be played using the inner 11x11 area with the outer lines serving as wraparound reference.

heading: Tournament History
content: On LittleGolem, an ongoing ladder tournament has 21 players. A previous tournament ran from 2012 to 2020: 129 players, 1,497 games, 138 rounds, average 76 moves per game. The European Go Congress has hosted toroidal Go tournaments, most recently in 2023.

heading: Standard 2-Player Halma

content: Once a piece has entered the opponent's camp, it may not leave. A piece that would move out of the opponent's camp is not permitted to do so.

heading: Winning

heading: Hex (13×13)
content: A larger board for deeper strategic play. With 169 cells, multiple independent fronts can develop simultaneously, making defensive play more viable and rewarding long-term positional thinking.

heading: Differences from Standard
content: Same rules as 11×11 Hex including swap rule. heading: Hex (14×14)
content: Alternative large-board format with 196 cells. Used in some international tournament settings as a compromise between the standard 11×11 and the marathon 19×19.

heading: Differences from Standard
content: Same rules as 11×11 Hex including swap rule. The even-numbered board size means neither player has an exact centre cell available, which subtly affects opening theory. Similar strategic depth to 13×13 with slightly longer games.

heading: Hex (19×19)
content: The largest standard board size with 361 cells matching Go's 19×19 intersection count. Games can run well over an hour and develop extraordinary complexity. Rarely used in competitive play due to time constraints, but available for those seeking maximum strategic depth.

heading: Differences from Standard
content: Same rules as 11×11 Hex including swap rule. heading: Hex (9×9)
content: A smaller board for quicker games. With 81 cells, games are more tactical than strategic and typically finish in 10-20 minutes. Popular for teaching Hex fundamentals and for rapid-play formats.

content: Same rules as 11×11 Hex. The reduced board size means that first-player advantage is more pronounced, making the swap rule especially important. heading: Hex (11×11)

content: Centre cells are strongest. The acute corners where your two edges are closest are critical defensive positions. Ladder formations, bridges two stones one apart that cannot both be blocked, and edge templates are fundamental tactical tools.

heading: Y
content: Invented by Claude Shannon and Craige Schensted in the 1950s. Played on a triangular board of hexagonal cells. Two players alternate placing stones. The first player to form a connected group touching all three edges of the triangle wins.

content: A triangular grid of hexagonal cells. Standard sizes range from side-length 9 to 15. Each edge of the triangle is one "side" — there are three sides total. Corner cells touch two edges simultaneously.

content: Y generalises the connection-win mechanic from "2 edges, each owned by a player" to "3 edges, first to touch all three". The engine's hasPath traversal needs to detect multi-target connectivity — not just "does a path exist from edge A to edge B" but "does a single group touch edges A AND B AND C".

heading: Differences from Standard Y
content: The larger board means single-edge contact is easy to achieve, but completing the three-edge connection requires sustained positional pressure. Defensive play is more viable at this scale. Games run considerably longer.

heading: Y (Small)
content: Compact Y variant for quicker games. The smaller triangular board makes three-edge connections achievable in fewer moves, putting more emphasis on tactical reading than long-range planning.

heading: Differences from Standard Y
content: With fewer cells, most moves are within reach of at least one edge, making early contact inevitable. Games are decided by which player can efficiently connect their scattered edge contacts through the interior. Ideal for teaching Y fundamentals or rapid-play formats.

content: Described in The Encyclopedia of Chess Variants by David Pritchard 1994. Also known as Cannibal Chess though that name more properly refers to the replacement variant where capturing substitutes movement rather than adding it. Public domain.

heading: Alice Chess
content: Invented by V. R. Parton in 1953. Named after Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass — pieces step through the mirror and emerge on the other side. Alice Chess uses two standard 8×8 chessboards played simultaneously.

heading: The Two Boards
content: Board A begins with the standard chess starting position. Board B begins empty. Boards share the same square coordinates. A piece on Board A at e4 and a piece on Board B at e4 occupy the same coordinate but are on different boards and do not interact directly.

heading: The Transfer Rule
content: After every move including captures, the piece that moved transfers to the corresponding square on the other board. - A piece on Board A at e4 transfers to Board B e4 after moving. - A piece on Board B at f6 transfers to Board A f6 after moving. A move is legal only if the transfer square is vacant.

heading: Setup
content: Board A: standard chess starting position. Board B: empty. All White and Black pieces begin on Board A.

heading: Physical Representation
content: Alice Chess is commonly played on a single physical board with a distinguishing marker — traditionally a checker piece placed underneath — to indicate which squares are Board B. heading: Overview

content: - If a pushed pawn reaches the last rank promotion rank, the pawn's owner chooses what piece it promotes to. - If the promotion results in a check against the player who did the pushing, that player loses immediately.

content: En passant captures are not used in Avalanche Chess.

heading: Overview
content: Byzantine Chess is a Shatranj variant popular in 10th-century Byzantium present-day Istanbul. It is played on a circular board of four concentric rings, each containing 16 squares, for 64 squares in total. The circular topology means file 16 p connects directly back to file 1 a around the ring.

heading: Capablanca Chess
content: Invented by World Champion José Raúl Capablanca in the 1920s to address what he saw as the "draw death" of standard chess. A larger board with two new compound pieces creates richer tactical possibilities.

heading: Setup
content: Board: 10×8 ten files, eight ranks. FEN: rnabqkbcnr/pppppppppp/10/10/10/10/PPPPPPPPPP/RNABQKBCNR w KQkq - 0 1

content: Pieces per side: Standard 16 pieces plus: - Archbishop ♗+♞ — combines Bishop and Knight movement. Placed between the Queen's Knight and Queen's Bishop. - Chancellor ♖+♞ — combines Rook and Knight movement. Placed between the King's Knight and King's Bishop. Setup from a-file: Rook, Knight, Archbisho

heading: Rules
content: Identical to standard chess with these additions: - Castling moves the King three squares toward the Rook to accommodate the wider board. - Pawns may promote to Archbishop or Chancellor in addition to standard pieces. - No en passant differences — same rules apply.

heading: Win Condition
content: Checkmate, same as standard chess.

heading: Strategy
content: The wider board and compound pieces create more open positions. The Archbishop dominates closed diagonals while the Chancellor controls open files with knight-fork threats. Pawn structure is more flexible with 10 files — flank play becomes viable alongside central control.

content: José Raúl Capablanca, c. 1920. Public domain.

heading: Overview
content: Carrera’s Chess extends standard chess to a 10×8 board by adding two compound pieces per side: the Champion Rook + Knight and the Centaur Bishop + Knight. It predates Capablanca’s Chess by three centuries and uses the same general concept.

heading: Setup
content: 10-file board files a–j, 8 ranks. The right corner on each player’s side is light-coloured. The Centaur is placed between the Rook and Knight on the Queen-side; the Champion is placed between the Knight and Rook on the King-side. heading: Champion (Campione)
content: Moves as a Rook slides orthogonally any distance or a Knight L-shape leap. Also known as Chancellor.

heading: Centaur (Centauro)
content: Moves as a Bishop slides diagonally any distance or a Knight L-shape leap. Also known as Archbishop. Not colour-bound due to the Knight component.

heading: No Castling
content: Castling is not used in Carrera’s Chess. Murray confirms Carrera followed Sicilian rules in which the King had no power to leap.

heading: No En Passant
content: En passant captures are not used. Italian Chess of Carrera’s era did not permit en passant.

heading: Restricted Pawn Double Move
content: Pawns may make an initial double-step move from their starting rank, with one restriction: a double move is forbidden if it would simultaneously block a check against the player’s own King AND would land on a square where an enemy Pawn in an adjacent file could capture it. content: A Pawn reaching the far rank promotes to a Queen. Whether promotion to Champion or Centaur is permitted is historically uncertain; playing promotion to Queen, Champion, or Centaur is recommended.

heading: Draw Conditions
content: Stalemate draw, insufficient mating material, perpetual check, threefold repetition, and the 50-move rule all apply as in modern chess.

heading: Modern Variant
content: Modern Carrera’s Chess uses the same setup but applies Capablanca’s Chess rules: castling is permitted King moves 3 squares toward the Rook, and promotion may include Champion and Centaur. Source: chessvariants.com/historic.dir/carrera.html

heading: Chennis
content: Designed by Corey Clark. Chennis adapts chess to a tennis-themed format on a 7×7 board. The net divides the board between ranks 4 and 5. Victory is achieved by getting a Pawn to the opponent’s back rank, not by checkmate — though check and piece capture remain mechanically active.

heading: Board Layout
content: The board is 7×7 files a–g, ranks 1–7. A net runs across the middle of the board, forming a barrier between ranks 4 and 5. This net restricts most pieces to their own half unless they can jump Knights or the rules explicitly permit crossing.

heading: Win Condition
content: The game is won by advancing any Pawn to the opponent’s back rank: - White wins by placing a Pawn on rank 7. - Black wins by placing a Pawn on rank 1. Checkmate is NOT a win condition in Chennis. However, check and piece capture are legal actions — they affect material balance and legal moves.

heading: Drops
content: Crazy 38's uses Shogi-style drops: instead of making a normal move, a player may drop any piece from their hand onto any vacant square, with the following restrictions: - A Pawn may not be dropped onto the opponent's Home Square. - A Pawn may not be dropped in a position that immediately checkmates

heading: Win Condition
content: A player wins by either: 1. Checkmating the opponent's King, or 2. Moving their own King onto the opponent's Home Square.

heading: Attribution
content: Crazy 38's was designed by Ben Good. Entry submitted to the 38 Squares Contest, January 1998. Source: chessvariants.com/38.dir/crazy/crazy38s.html

heading: Crazyhouse
content: Captured pieces join the captor's reserve. Instead of moving, you may drop a piece from your hand onto any empty square. The most popular chess variant online.

heading: Win Condition
content: Checkmate the opponent's King.

heading: Strategy
content: Piece drops create explosive tactical possibilities — no piece is ever truly lost. Material advantage matters less than board control and king safety. Early attacks are common because captured pieces immediately reinforce the attack. Pawn structure is less important since pawns can appear anywhere.

heading: Attribution
content: Traditional variant. Derives from Shogi's drop mechanic applied to Western chess. Popularised on Lichess and FICS. Public domain.

heading: Cylinder Chess
content: The board wraps horizontally, forming a cylinder. The a-file is adjacent to the h-file.

content: Board: Standard 8×8 files wrap. Setup: Standard chess setup. FEN: rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1

content: - The a-file connects to the h-file. heading: Win Condition
content: Checkmate the opponent's King.

heading: Strategy
content: Bishops become much more powerful on a cylinder — they can reach every square of their colour. Rook files are no longer safe flanks since attacks can come from behind via the wrap. Flank pawns gain additional capture options. The lack of board edges eliminates many standard endgame techniques.

heading: Attribution
content: Traditional variant with roots in 19th-century chess composition. Public domain.

heading: Overview
content: Cylindrical Chess is played on a standard 8×8 board, but the board is treated as a cylinder: the left and right edges are connected. File a is adjacent to file h. A piece that moves off one edge of the board reappears from the other side.

content: All standard FIDE rules apply with the following modifications for the cylindrical board:

content: All pieces may move and attack across the board edge. heading: En Passant
content: En passant works normally across the cylinder. For example: if White has a pawn on a5 and Black plays h7–h5, White may capture en passant with a5×h6.

heading: Castling
content: Castling is permitted under standard FIDE conditions. The Rook does not cross the board edge during castling — only standard castling not over the edge is allowed.

heading: Null Moves
content: A piece may not make a null move — it cannot travel all the way around the board to return to its starting square. Such moves are only allowed in some problem contexts.

heading: Stalemate
content: Stalemate is a draw, as in standard chess.

heading: Strategy Notes
content: Piece values are significantly different from standard chess: Bishops are considerably stronger than in standard chess because they can reach more squares via the wrap. Queens gain even more. Knights and Rooks benefit only modestly. Center control is less important — advancing a central pawn exposes

heading: Dark Chess
content: The most restrictive fog variant. Each player can ONLY see squares occupied by their own pieces — not squares they attack. Chess becomes a game of memory, deduction, and blind aggression.

heading: Setup
content: Board: Standard 8×8, but each player's view is severely limited. Setup: Standard chess starting position. FEN: rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1

content: Visibility: - You can ONLY see squares occupied by your own pieces. - All other squares are invisible — you cannot see enemy pieces or empty squares. - When you move a piece, you discover what is on the destination square only upon arrival. content: Capture the opponent's King.

content: Information is almost nonexistent. You must remember where enemy pieces were last seen when you occupied adjacent squares. content: Modern variant. Distinguished from Fog of War by its stricter visibility rules. Public domain.

heading: De Vasa's Hexagonal Chess

content: Two dice are rolled each turn instead of one. heading: Diana Chess

heading: Displacement Chess

content: Checkmate the opponent's King.

content: Swaps enable rapid piece coordination — a trapped rook can swap with an adjacent pawn to escape. The King can dodge threats by swapping with a defender. Development becomes faster since pieces can be repositioned without spending multiple tempi. Watch for swap-based discovered attacks.

heading: Fog of War Chess

content: Captures create a defensive shield around the victim's neighbours — making exchanges near clustered pieces dangerous. heading: Racing Kings
content: No checks allowed. Race your King to rank 8. A pure positional race with no violence.

heading: Setup

heading: Rules
content: - No move may give check to either King. Any move that would place either King in check is illegal. - No castling. No pawns. No pawn promotion.

heading: Win Condition
content: First player to move their King to rank 8 wins. If White reaches rank 8, Black gets one more move — if Black also reaches rank 8, the game is a draw.

heading: Strategy
content: Block your opponent's King path while clearing your own. Rooks and Queens control files; Bishops control diagonals. The constraint against giving check makes many "obvious" blocking moves illegal.

heading: Piece Movement

heading: Rook
content: Slides any number of squares along a single axis rank, file, or level. Cannot jump over pieces. In 3D space the Rook has 6 orthogonal sliding directions ±rank, ±file, ±level.

heading: Bishop
content: Slides any number of squares along a two-axis diagonal rank+file, rank+level, or file+level, in any combination of signs. Cannot jump over pieces. In 3D space the Bishop has 12 diagonal sliding directions.

heading: Unicorn (U)

heading: Queen
content: Combines the Rook and Bishop orthogonal and two-axis diagonal slides. Does not include the Unicorn's triagonal move. Cannot jump over pieces.

heading: Knight
content: Leaps to any square exactly 2 steps in one axis and 1 step in another the standard chess knight jump, extended to 3D. This gives up to 24 destinations from a central square. Always jumps over intervening pieces.

heading: King
content: Moves one step in any direction — orthogonal, two-axis diagonal, or triagonal — giving up to 26 possible destinations from an interior square. Cannot move into check.

heading: Recruitment Chess

heading: Rifle Chess

content: Pieces become much harder to dislodge since capturing doesn't occupy their square. Batteries multiple pieces lined up are devastating because a front piece can "shoot" without opening the line. The value of centralisation increases enormously.

heading: Shah Exchange
content: Once per game, when a player's Shah is in check or stalemate, that player may swap the Shah with any other friendly piece on the board. The swap constitutes the player's entire move for that turn.

heading: Citadel Draw
content: If a player moves their Shah into the citadel square on the opponent's side of the board, the game is immediately a draw. heading: Tandem Chess
content: Tandem Chess also known as Siamese Chess is a 4-player team chess variant played on two simultaneous standard boards. It is closely related to Bughouse Chess and shares most of its rules, with two key distinctions. It is one of the most widely played team chess formats internationally.

heading: Setup
content: Two standard 8×8 boards: - Board A: White1 Team A vs Black1 Team B - Board B: White2 Team A vs Black2 Team B Teams: White1 + White2 vs Black1 + Black2. Partners sit on the same side of the table. On each board, one team member plays White and the other plays Black.

heading: The Relay Mechanic
content: When a player captures an enemy piece, it is passed to their partner on the other board. The partner may drop place the received piece onto any empty square on their board in lieu of making a normal move. Drop restrictions: - A Pawn may not be dropped on the 1st or 8th rank. - A piece may not be dro

heading: Win Condition
content: The match continues until both boards have been completed not just the first checkmate. After both games end, the score is counted: - 1 point for a win on a board - ½ point for a draw - 0 points for a loss The team with the higher total score wins. If teams score 1–1, the match is a draw.

heading: Turn Order
content: Play proceeds as in standard chess on each board — White1 and Black1 alternate on Board A; White2 and Black2 alternate on Board B. Partners may not advise each other, but may request a specific piece type e.g., "Partner, I need a Knight".

heading: Key Differences from Bughouse Chess
content: Tandem Chess differs from Bughouse in two rules: 1. No check or checkmate by drop — dropped pieces may not place the enemy King in check. 2. Both games must complete — the match is not decided by the first checkmate; both boards are played to completion.

heading: Strategy
content: Teleports are powerful but finite; save them for decisive moments. Common uses: teleporting a Knight or Queen into a mating net, escaping a trapped piece, or repositioning the King to safety. Bluffing with teleport availability adds a psychological dimension.

content: - Checkmate as normal, OR - Deliver check three times. Each check is counted regardless of whether it was blocked, evaded, or interposed.

content: Pieces that give check frequently Queen, Bishops on open diagonals become much more valuable. Sacrificing material to deliver checks becomes a core tactic. Defensive play must prioritise minimising the number of times the King is checked, not just surviving.

heading: Jieqi

content: The board, palace, river, and starting positions are identical to standard Xiangqi. heading: Blinded
content: - A blinded creature can't see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.

heading: Charmed
content: - A charmed creature can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects.

heading: Deafened
content: - A deafened creature can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.

heading: Frightened
content: - A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.

heading: Grappled
content: - A grappled creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.

heading: Incapacitated
content: - An incapacitated creature can't take actions or reactions.

heading: Invisible

heading: Paralyzed
content: - A paralyzed creature is incapacitated (see the condition) and can't move or speak.

heading: Petrified
content: - A petrified creature is transformed, along with any nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it cea

heading: Poisoned
content: - A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

heading: Prone
content: - A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.

heading: Restrained
content: - A restrained creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.

heading: Stunned
content: - A stunned creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move, and can speak only falteringly.

heading: Unconscious
content: - An unconscious creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.

heading: Demon, Nalfeshnee
content: A towering, corpulent beast, this fiend has the hideous head of a boar and arms ending in fatty, four-fingered hands.

heading: Demon, Quasit
content: Ram horns curl back from the twisted head of this tiny winged demon, and its body is thin and wiry.

heading: Demon, Shadow
content: Only this shadowy bat-winged demon's teeth and claws have any sense of physicality to them—the rest is lost in darkness.

heading: Demon, Succubus
content: Tiny horns, bat-like wings, and a sinuous tail betray the demonic nature of this alluring woman.

heading: Demon, Vrock
content: A cloud of spores and a trail of feathers surrounds this twisted cross between a man and a gigantic vulture.

heading: Derro
content: This pale blue humanoid has bulging white eyes, wild hair, four-fingered hands, and a large hooked club.

heading: Devil, Barbed
content: From the tip of its lashing tail to the serrated features of its fang-filled visage, this fiery-eyed sentinel bristles with barbs.

heading: Devil, Bearded
content: This seething devil deftly wields a vicious, saw-toothed glaive, while below its toothy maw writhes a hideous, twitching beard.

heading: Devil, Bone
content: Merging the most horrifying features of carrion-fed insect and withered cadaver, this bony devil moves in unsettling lurches.

heading: Devil, Erinyes
content: Some calamity has befallen this angelic warrior. Wings stained black shear the air as her merciless eyes search for a target.

heading: Devil, Horned
content: Bristling with terrible spines and a crown of deadly horns, this leering winged terror wields a whirling barbed chain.

heading: Devil, Ice
content: A pair of frozen, multifaceted eyes coldly judge all before this towering, insectile monstrosity.

heading: Devil, Imp
content: Fiendish wings and a whipping scorpion-like tail lash behind this diminutive, red-skinned nuisance.

heading: Devil, Lemure
content: A roiling wave of flesh gushes forward. Amid the fatty surge wriggle half-formed limbs and a dripping tumorous face.

heading: Devourer
content: This dry, hovering corpse's chest is a prison of jagged ribs, within which is trapped a small tormented ghostly form.

heading: Dinosaur, Ankylosaurus
content: Thick bony plates armor the domelike back of this quadrupedal dinosaur, its powerfully muscled tail ending in a bony club.

heading: Dinosaur, Brachiosaurus
content: A long tail counterbalances this reptile's equally long neck, at the end of which a relatively small head pulls food from the treetop.

heading: Dinosaur, Deinonychus
content: This brightly colored dinosaur exudes a dangerous ferocity. Each foot is armed with a large, sickle-shaped claw.

heading: Dinosaur, Elasmosaurus
content: Long-necked and long-tailed, this large, predatory reptile glides through the water on four powerful flippers.

heading: Dinosaur, Pteranodon
content: This flying reptile has two huge wings and a distinctive backward-sweeping crest decorating its head.

heading: Dinosaur, Stegosaurus
content: This huge dinosaur has a small head, twin rows of sharp dorsal plates, and a muscular tail terminating in a set of bony spikes.

heading: Dinosaur, Triceratops
content: This beast's armored head has three sharp horns decorating its face and a large round crest angling back over its neck from its skull.

heading: Dinosaur, Tyrannosaurus
content: This bipedal dinosaur's front arms seem small compared to the rest of its bulk, but its enormous head is all teeth.

heading: Dog
content: Dog Animal

heading: Dog, Riding
content: This burly dog is fitted with a small saddle. A low, menacing growl rumbles up from its chest.

heading: Dolphin
content: This streamlined, fish-like mammal has sparkling eyes over a smiling mouth filled with hundreds of teeth.

heading: Dolphin, Orca
content: This sleek black whale has a distinctive white patch near each eye and a mouth filled with sharp teeth.

heading: Doppelganger
content: This grayish humanoid creature seems almost unfinished, with a narrow head, gaunt limbs, and a sinister, noseless face.

heading: Dracolisk
content: This six-legged dragon flaps its massive wings as it lowers its head to glare with hideous glowing eyes.

heading: Drider
content: The dry rasping of spidery legs brings this hideous monstrosity into view—a nightmarish, centaurian fusion of drow and spider.

heading: Drow
content: This dark-skinned elf stands in a battle-ready pose, her hair silver and eyes white and pupilless.

heading: Drow Noble
content: Drow Noble Humanoid

heading: Dryad
content: This strange, beautiful woman has flesh that seems made of wood and vibrant hair that resembles leaves and blossoms.

heading: Duergar
content: This bald, long-bearded dwarf has dull gray skin, low arching brows, and eyes that seem to absorb rather than reflect the light.

heading: Eagle
content: This magnificent bird of prey has dark feathers save for those on its head, which are pure white.

heading: Eagle, Giant
content: This immense eagle's feathers are golden brown and shimmer in the light. Its sharp beak and curved talons are dark yellow.

heading: Eel, Electric
content: This six-foot-long, snake-like fish moves slowly. A strange popping and snapping sound occasionally emits from the creature's body.

heading: Eel, Giant Moray
content: This sixteen-foot-long eel slithers through the water with uncanny grace, mouth open to display large teeth and a second set of jaws.

heading: Elephant, Mastodon
content: This creature is larger than a normal elephant, with enormous sweeping tusks and shaggy brown fur on its body.

heading: Ettercap
content: This hideous purple creature walks upright like a man, but its face is that of a spider, and its hands are sickle-shaped claws.

heading: Ettin
content: This lumbering, filthy, two-headed giant wears tattered remnants of leather armor and clutches a large flail in each fist.

heading: Dragon Turtle
content: This long-tailed aquatic beast resembles a massive snapping turtle with draconic features.

heading: Flytrap, Giant
content: This towering plant is a mass of vines and barbs. Several stalks are horribly mobile, each ending in a set of green, toothy jaws.

heading: Frog, Giant
content: This creature looks like a normal frog, with moist, mottled, blackish-green skin, but grown to truly monstrous size.

heading: Frog, Poison
content: This small frog is bright green and red, with electric-blue stripes on its hind legs.

heading: Froghemoth
content: This immense, three-eyed frog-like creature rears up on powerful hind legs. In place of arms, four huge tentacles thrash and writhe.

heading: Gargoyle
content: Seemingly carved from a dark gray stone, this sinister crouching humanoid resembles a horned, winged demon.

heading: Gelatinous Cube
content: Bits of broken weapons, coins, and a partially digested skeleton are visible inside this quivering cube of slime.

heading: Genie, Djinni
content: This creature stands nearly twice as tall as a human, although its lower torso trails away into a vortex of mist and wind.

heading: Genie, Efreeti
content: This muscular giant has crimson skin, smoldering eyes, and small black horns. Smoke rises in curls from its flesh.

heading: Genie, Janni
content: This regal figure looks like a tall, well-proportioned human, save that its eyes sparkle with strange light.

heading: Genie, Marid
content: This being resembles a powerful giant with hairless blue-green skin, deep blue eyes, flamboyant eyebrows, and pearlescent teeth.

heading: Genie, Shaitan
content: This being resembles a towering human with skin of polished stone and glittering agate eyes.

heading: Ghost
content: This spectral, horrifying figure glides silently through the air, passing through solid objects as if they didn't exist. This sample ghost is built from a 7th-level human aristocrat — the spirit of a

heading: Ghoul
content: This humanoid creature has long, sharp teeth, and its pallid flesh is stretched tightly over its starved frame.

heading: Giant, Cloud
content: This towering giant has finely chiseled features. Her skin is pale and smooth, and her long wispy hair flutters as if in a breeze.

heading: Giant, Fire
content: This lumbering giant has short stumpy legs and powerful, muscular arms. Its hair and beard seem to be made of fire.

heading: Giant, Frost
content: This giant looks like a thick, muscular human. It has frost-white skin and long, light blue hair that it wears braided.

heading: Giant, Hill
content: This hunched giant exudes power and a crude, stupid anger, its filthy fur clothing bespeaking a brutish and backwoods lifestyle.

heading: Giant, Stone
content: This giant has chiseled, muscular features and a flat, forward-sloping head, looking almost as if it were carved of stone.

heading: Giant, Storm
content: This giant is a towering, muscular human of heroic proportions, with bronze skin, dark hair, and sparkling green eyes.

heading: Gibbering Mouther
content: This horrid mass of eyes, mouths, and formless flesh stares in all directions, its countless maws yammering ceaselessly.

heading: Girallon
content: This four-armed, gorilla-like creature, covered with matted white fur, roars in rage as it rears up to its full, towering height.

heading: Gnoll
content: Hunched and feral, this furred, hyena-headed humanoid stands slightly taller than the average human.

heading: Goblin
content: This creature stands barely three feet tall, its scrawny, humanoid body dwarfed by its wide, ungainly head.

heading: Goblin Dog
content: This mangy canine's face has the same flat nose, beady eyes, and protruding teeth as a rat grown grotesquely large.

heading: Golem, Clay
content: A clay golem wears no clothing except for a metal or stiff leather garment around its hips. It stands over 8 feet tall and weighs 600 pounds.

heading: Golem, Flesh
content: A flesh golem is a ghoulish collection of stolen humanoid body parts, stitched together into a single composite form. Its cadaverous flesh has a sickly green or yellowish tint. A flesh golem wears wha

heading: Golem, Ice
content: Ice golems are humanoid automatons formed of carved ice. Their appearance can range from roughly chiseled figures of ice and snow to elaborately detailed ice sculptures and beautiful crystalline statu

heading: Golem, Iron
content: An iron golem has a humanoid body made from iron. It can be sculpted into any shape its creator desires, but it almost always displays armor of some sort, from simple and utilitarian to ceremonial and

heading: Golem, Stone
content: A stone golem has a humanoid body made from stone, frequently stylized to suit its creator. For example, it might look like it is wearing armor, with a particular symbol carved on the breastplate, or

heading: Golem, Wood
content: A wood golem is carved from rare woods, assembled into a roughly humanoid body with articulated limbs. Their creators usually leave their bodies almost unfinished, with individual pieces of lumber and

heading: Gorgon
content: This bull-like creature seems to be made of interlocking metallic plates. Faint plumes of green smoke puff from its mouth.

heading: Gray Ooze
content: A seemingly mundane puddle, patch of moist stone, or glistening rock is suddenly revealed to be more as a terrible pseudopod lashes out.

heading: Green Hag
content: Knots of dark, moldering hair spill over the features of this sickly, thin, green-skinned crone.

heading: Griffon
content: This majestic beast has the body of a lion, the head and forelegs of a great eagle, and a massive pair of feathered wings.

heading: Harpy
content: Save for the tattered wings and taloned feet, this creature resembles a feral woman with a wild look about her.

heading: Hell Hound
content: This creature resembles a thin, lanky wolf with reddish-brown fur, white claws, and burning, fiery red eyes.

heading: Hell Hound, Nessian
content: This creature resembles a powerfully built wolf the size of a large draft horse, with ebony fur and burning, fiery red eyes.

heading: Herd Animal, Aurochs
content: This large, horned bull has a dirty black hide and an aggressive temper. Its horns are wide and sharp.

heading: Herd Animal, Bison
content: This creature has small, upward-pointing horns, a shaggy coat of fur, and a large hump on its shoulders.

heading: Hobgoblin
content: Standing as tall as a human, this muscular, gray-skinned creature peers about with tiny, observant eyes.

heading: Homunculus
content: This vaguely humanoid creature is about the size of a cat but looks more like a toothy, winged devil.

heading: Horse
content: This proud horse thunders across the grassy plain with fluid grace, wind tugging at its loose-fitting barding.

heading: Horse, Pony
content: This squat equine plods forward with large, curious eyes. As it nears, it extends its muzzle, clearly expecting a treat.

heading: Human Skeleton
content: Human Skeleton Undead

heading: Human Zombie
content: Human Zombie Undead

heading: Hydra
content: Multiple angry snake-like heads rise from the sleek, serpentine body of this terrifying monster.

heading: Hyena
content: This hyena is covered in shaggy, tan-colored fur with black and brown stripes.

heading: Hyena, Dire
content: This large hyena has a thick head, rheumy red eyes, and a mouth filled with sharp, powerful teeth.

heading: Intellect Devourer
content: Devoid of a head, or any features at all save for four short, clawed legs, this creature's body looks like a large, glistening brain.

heading: Invisible Stalker
content: No true form can be detected, yet a sense of force and hulking malevolence is undeniable in this creature's presence.

heading: Iron Cobra
content: This creature resembles a small, metallic cobra. Its body is made of overlapping iron plates, and its eyes are pinpoints of red light.

heading: Kobold
content: This short, reptilian humanoid has scaled skin, a snout filled with tiny teeth, and a long tail.

heading: Kraken
content: This tremendous leviathan resembles a vast squid, yet the markings on its body are strangely unsettling to look upon.

heading: Kyton
content: Wickedly barbed chains adorn this lean figure, and gaps in the bindings reveal deathly pale flesh etched with jagged scars.

heading: Lamia
content: This creature's upper torso is that of a comely woman with cat's eyes and sharp fangs, while her lower body is that of a lion.

heading: Leech, Giant
content: A parasite ballooned to monstrous proportions undulates in the muck, its circular maw a spiral of teeth.

heading: Lich
content: Once fine robes hang in tatters from this withered corpse's frame. A pale blue light shines from where its eyes should be.

heading: Linnorm, Crag
content: This immense, wingless dragon rears up on a serpentine body. Its triple tail and powerful talons swipe at the air.

heading: Linnorm, Ice
content: A snake-like, dragon-headed monster of tremendous size rises up, drifts of snow and ice tumbling from its coiling flanks.

heading: Linnorm, Tarn
content: This nightmarishly huge, snake-like dragon possesses two equally fearsome heads. Its twin jaws seethe with acid and poison.

heading: Lion
content: This great cat's muscles flex visibly under its skin as it bares its fangs and shakes its thick mane of hair.

heading: Lion, Dire
content: This immense spotted lion stands as tall as a man at the shoulder, its fur matted with the blood of its victims.

heading: Lizard, Giant Frilled
content: This bright-eyed lizard is larger than a horse. As it hisses in anger, a brightly colored frill extends around its neck.

heading: Lizard, Monitor
content: This immense lizard moves with a slow but relentless gait. Its feet end in large talons, and ropes of drool hang from its toothy maw.

heading: Lizardfolk
content: This reptilian humanoid has green scales, a short and toothy snout, and a thick alligator-like tail.

heading: Manticore
content: This creature has a vaguely humanoid head, the body of a lion, and the wings of a dragon. Its tail ends in long, sharp spikes.

heading: Mantis, Giant
content: This towering insect walks on its back four legs. Its head is triangular and its front legs sport razor-sharp edges and claws.

heading: Medusa
content: This slender, attractive woman has strangely glowing eyes and a full head of hissing snakes for hair.

heading: Mephit, Air
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Dust
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Earth
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Fire
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Ice
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Magma
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Ooze
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Salt
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Steam
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Mephit, Water
content: This small humanoid creature has thin, leathery wings, small horns, and a mischievous smile.

heading: Merfolk
content: Slipping in and out of the crashing waves, this beautiful woman has the lower torso of a long, slender fish.

heading: Mimic
content: What appeared to be a chest filled with treasure comes to life as it grows long, glistening tentacles and a number of sharp teeth.

heading: Minotaur
content: With the body of a powerfully built man and the head of a snarling bull, this creature stomps its hooves as if preparing to charge.

heading: Mite
content: This squat humanoid seems to be nearly all head—an unfortunate circumstance, considering how ugly its puffy blue face is.

heading: Mohrg
content: A thick tangle of discolored entrails clings to this lurching skeleton's torso and winds upward to loll from its jaw like a clawed tongue.

heading: Morlock
content: Skin pale as a slug's belly, eyes huge and bulging, this thing crawls down the wall like a spider, but its shape is hideously humanoid.

heading: Mummy
content: Wrapped from head to toe in ancient strips of moldering linen, this humanoid moves with a shuffling gait.

heading: Naga, Dark
content: A sharp-featured humanoid head crowns the powerful, sinuous body of this snake-like monstrosity.

heading: Naga, Guardian
content: A contemplative humanoid face framed by a cobra-like hood adorns the body of this long, brightly colored serpent.

heading: Naga, Spirit
content: Yellowed, venom-dripping fangs fill the human-like mouth of this sinister serpentine monstrosity.

heading: Neothelid
content: Its slime-drenched length coiled upon itself in a shuddering mountain, this huge worm's tentacled head rises like a snake's.

heading: Night Hag
content: Grisly fetishes and the rags of once fine clothes hang off the corpse-thin frame of this horrifying, sharp-fanged crone.

heading: Nightmare
content: This eerie horse-like creature's skin is an inky blackness. Fire spurts from its hair and nostrils, and its hooves spray sparks.

heading: Nightmare, Cauchemar
content: This towering, burning equine stands upon smoking hooves. Hellfire shimmers in its hateful eyes.

heading: Nymph
content: A delicate figure rises from the water, her long ears tapering to points above her head, her beauty painful in its perfection.

heading: Ochre Jelly
content: This yellow-orange amoeboid creature slithers across the ground, pseudopods grasping ahead of its slow approach.

heading: Octopus
content: Eight tentacles, each adorned with rows of countless suckers, unfurl from the barrel-shaped body of this large-eyed creature.

heading: Octopus, Giant
content: A storm of tentacles, each twenty feet in length, flails with deadly precision from the leathery body of this gigantic octopus.

heading: Ogre
content: This lumbering giant's beady eyes are devoid of wit or kindness, and its puffy face features a wide mouth with ill-fitting teeth.

heading: Oni, Ogre Mage
content: Clad in beautiful armor, this exotically garbed giant roars, its tusks glistening and its eyes afire with murderous intent.

heading: Orc
content: This savage creature looks like a bestial version of a savage human, with green-gray skin and greasy black hair.

heading: Otyugh
content: This three-legged freak is mostly mouth. Three tentacles, two tipped with barbs and one with eyes, extend from its sides.

heading: Owlbear
content: An amalgam of fur and feathers, this bizarre half-bear, half-owl monstrosity raises its huge, ursine claws in anger.

heading: Pegasus
content: This magnificient horse has great bird-like wings upon its back and moves with a quiet and proud grace.

heading: Phase Spider
content: This large spider-like monster has an eerie, humanoid face surrounded by a shaggy mane of fur.

heading: Phoenix
content: This immense bird seems to be made of living flame. It spreads its wings and gives vent to a musical cry as it takes to the air.

heading: Pit Fiend
content: Pit Fiend Outsider

heading: Pixie
content: This tiny, whimsical-looking humanoid darts about swiftly on wildly colored gossamer wings.

heading: Pseudodragon
content: This housecat-sized miniature dragon has fine scales, sharp horns, wicked little teeth, and a tail tipped with a barbed stinger.

heading: Purple Worm
content: This enormous worm is covered with dark purple plates of chitinous armor. Its giant, tooth-filled mouth is the size of an ox.

heading: Rakshasa
content: This figure's backward-bending fingers and its bestial, snarling visage leave little doubt as to its fiendish nature.

heading: Rat, Dire
content: This filthy rat is the size of a small dog. It has a coat of coarse fur, a long and scabby tail, and two glittering eyes.

heading: Remorhaz
content: An immense centipede-like beast erupts from the snow, rows of chitinous plates on its back glowing red-hot.

heading: Retriever
content: A spider the size of a bull elephant rears up on its back four legs in a violent challenge, eyes shimmering with magical energy.

heading: Rhinoceros
content: This rhinoceros has a low-slung head with twisted ears that lie back along its neck.

heading: Rhinoceros, Woolly
content: This large rhinoceros has a shaggy pelt of long, brown fur and a row of immense horns on its snout and brow.

heading: Roc
content: This immense raptor unleashes a shrill cry as it bares its talons, each large enough to carry off a horse.

heading: Roper
content: A huge eye opens in this conical creature's front, just above a toothy mouth. Long strands of fibrous material whip from its sides.

heading: Rust Monster
content: This insectile monster has four legs, a strange propeller-shaped protrusion at the end of its tail, and two long, feathery antennae.

heading: Sahuagin
content: This scaly humanoid has a long, fish-like tail. Its arms and legs end in webbed claws, and its piscine head features a toothy maw.

heading: Salamander
content: This snake-bodied humanoid hisses with anger. Spines of crackling flame dance along the creature's blackened, fiery-red scales.

heading: Satyr
content: This handsome, grinning man has the furry legs of a goat and a set of curling ram horns extending from his temples.

heading: Scorpion, Giant
content: The sixteen-foot-long scorpion scrabbles forward, ferocious claws raised in challenge, stingered tail arched over its back.

heading: Sea Hag
content: Hair like rotting seaweed drapes this ancient witch. Loose, algae-colored skin sags off her starved frame.

heading: Sea Serpent
content: Spine-frilled neck arching up from the water like a snake ready to strike, this ship-sized serpent hisses a challenge.

heading: Shadow
content: Barely seen out of the corner of the eye, this wisp of shadow is vaguely humanoid in outline and writhes with unholy life.

heading: Shadow, Greater
content: This shadowy figure sways and moves with an erratic grace, as if lit by an unseen fire.

heading: Shambling Mound
content: A mass of tangled vines and dripping slime rises on two trunk-like legs, reeking of rot and freshly turned earth.

heading: Shark
content: This blue shark's fins slice through the water, its black eyes rolling and its gaping jaws showing countless teeth.

heading: Shark, Dire
content: Large as a dragon, this shark's jaws open to reveal a cavernous, tooth-lined gullet capable of swallowing a horse whole.

heading: Shocker Lizard
content: This dog-sized lizard has two horns, one on either side of its head, and green scales that crackle with sparks of lightning.

heading: Shoggoth
content: This immense mound of black slime thunders forward, eyes and mouths and even stranger things forming in its heaving bulk.

heading: Skeletal Champion
content: This armored skeleton stands in a battle-ready pose, its weapon held high as cold blue light shines in its eye sockets.

heading: Skum
content: This hunchbacked, green-skinned humanoid has a wide, frog-like head but a mouth more akin to that of a toothy fish.

heading: Slug, Giant
content: This massive, gray-brown slug leaves a viscous trail of slime in its wake as a long rasping tongue tastes the air for prey.

heading: Snake, Constrictor
content: This large snake has a thick, muscular body and dull green scales decorated with dirty brown stripes.

heading: Snake, Venomous
content: This brightly colored snake assumes an aggressive posture, its hissing mouth open to display its fangs.

heading: Spectre
content: This translucent, ghostly figure fades into view from the damp mist, its face distorted by wrath into a hideous mask.

heading: Sphinx
content: This creature has the body of a lion, the wings of a falcon, and the head and torso of a beautiful human woman.

heading: Spider, Giant
content: A spider the size of a man crawls silently from the depths of its funnel-shaped web.

heading: Squid
content: This slender red squid darts through the water with alacrity. Two large eyes stare from above the creature's tentacles.

heading: Squid, Giant
content: Immense in size, this great squid's tentacles writhe and flash with almost nauseating speed. The beast's eyes are as big as shields.

heading: Stirge
content: This insectoid creature has two pairs of bat wings, a tangle of thin legs, and a needle-sharp proboscis.

heading: Svirfneblin
content: This bald gnome has rocky gray skin and a wiry physique. Its pale eyes are overly large and expressive.

heading: Swarm, Army Ant
content: A writhing carpet of ants seethes over the ground, consuming everything in its path.

heading: Swarm, Bat
content: Hundreds of high-pitched squeaks fill the air as a mass of small, carnivorous bats surges forth, all of them hungry for blood.

heading: Swarm, Centipede
content: A writhing mass of legs and poisonous pincers swarms across the ground in a deadly, undulating wave.

heading: Swarm, Crab
content: A writhing mass of clacking shells and snapping pincers rushes from the surf, their spider-like legs twitching across the sand.

heading: Swarm, Leech
content: A mass of wriggling black creatures each the size of a man's finger stirs the stagnant water before enveloping its victim.

heading: Swarm, Rat
content: A squirming, roiling mass of squeaking rats draws closer, teeth flashing and claws scratching everything in its path.

heading: Swarm, Spider
content: An awful, scuttling mass of legs and mandibles scrambles forward out of the darkness.

heading: Swarm, Wasp
content: A low, ominous buzz announces the arrival of a mass of many thousands of angry, stinging wasps.

heading: Tarrasque
content: This immense reptilian beast towers over the surroundings like a dinosaur, all teeth and horns and claws and thrashing spiked tail.

heading: Tengu
content: Black feathers cover this crow-headed humanoid, and its hands and legs end in powerful talons.

heading: Tiefling
content: This lanky man sneers as he draws his sword. Tiny horns and a barbed tail reveal that he is something more than human.

heading: Tiger
content: This powerful feline predator moves with a deadly grace, its reddish-orange fur slashed with black stripes.

heading: Tiger, Dire
content: This large tiger grumbles a warning as it crouches. Two saber-like fangs jut downward from its powerful jaws.

heading: Treant
content: This animated tree's bark is knotted into vaguely humanoid features, with branches for arms and roots for legs.

heading: Troglodyte
content: This humanoid's scaly hide is dull gray. Its frame resembles that of a cave lizard, with a long tail and crests on its head and back.

heading: Troll
content: This tall creature has rough, green hide. Its hands end in claws, and its bestial face has a hideous, tusked underbite.

heading: Unicorn
content: This magnificent beast looks like a white horse, but with a goat's beard and a single long ivory horn on its brow.

heading: Vampire
content: This alluring, raven-haired beauty casually wipes a trickle of blood from a pale cheek, then smiles to reveal needle-sharp fangs.

heading: Vargouille
content: This creature is a blackened, bat-winged fiend's head. Tentacles dangle from chin and scalp, and its fanged mouth hangs agape.

heading: Vegepygmy
content: Short, thin, and green, this small humanoid wields a spear. Tendrils of fungus dangle from its arms, midsection, and legs.

heading: Violet Fungus
content: This mushroom grows from a bed of tentacular roots. Deep violet tendrils slither out of the dozens of fissures in its pointed cap.

heading: Wasp, Giant
content: This horse-sized wasp is covered in yellow and black vertical stripes—its stinger is the size of a sword and drips with venom.

content: Wererat Humanoid

heading: Werewolf
content: Werewolf Humanoid

heading: Wight
content: The flesh of this walking corpse is rotting and putrid, its body skeletal in places and its eye sockets glowing with red light.

heading: Wolf
content: This powerful canine watches its prey with piercing yellow eyes, darting its tongue across sharp white teeth.

heading: Wolf, Dire
content: This immense black wolf is the size of a horse, its fangs as large and sharp as knives.

heading: Wolverine
content: This stocky, muscular mammal is the size of a badger, its snarling lips revealing a mouth full of yellow teeth.

heading: Wolverine, Dire
content: This terrible wolverine is as large as a bear, its jaws and claws oversized and brutal, its eyes dark and filled with rage.

heading: Worg
content: This unusually large wolf has an evil, almost intelligent light shining in its deep red eyes.

heading: Worg, Winter Wolf
content: This bear-sized wolf has white fur and a rime of frost around its muzzle. Its eyes are pale blue, almost white in color.

heading: Wraith
content: This ghostly creature is little more than a dark shape with two flickering pinpoints of light where its eyes should be.

heading: Wyvern
content: A dark blue dragon, its wings immense and its tail tipped with a hooked stinger, lands on two taloned feet and roars a challenge.

heading: Xill
content: This flame-red humanoid appears to be a strange mix of insect and reptile, with four arms and twitching, fanged mandibles.

heading: Xorn
content: This squat beast is as wide as it is tall. Strangely symmetrical, it has three arms, three legs, three eyes, and one huge mouth.

heading: Yellow Musk Creeper
content: Coiling around several human skeletons, this wet green plant's sickly flowers smoke with a nasty yellow vapor.

heading: Yeth Hound
content: This emaciated, hairless canine has a strange air of menace and cruelty about it.

heading: Yeti
content: This creature stands like a man, yet is half again the height of most men and covered with a coat of thick white fur.

heading: Banded Mail
content: Banded mail is made up of overlapping strips of metal, fastened to a leather backing. The suit includes gauntlets.

heading: Breastplate
content: Covering only the torso, a breastplate is made up of a single piece of sculpted metal.

heading: Buckler

heading: Chain Shirt
content: Covering the torso, this shirt is made up of thousands of interlocking metal rings.

heading: Chainmail
content: Unlike a chain shirt, chainmail covers the legs and arms of the wearer. The suit includes gauntlets.

heading: Full Plate

heading: Gauntlet, Locked

heading: Half-Plate
content: Combining elements of full plate and chainmail, half-plate includes gauntlets and a helm.

heading: Hide
content: Hide armor is made up of the tanned and preserved skin of any thick-hided beast.

heading: Leather
content: Leather armor is made up of pieces of hard boiled leather carefully sewn together.

heading: Padded
content: Little more than heavy, quilted cloth, this armor provides only the most basic protection.

heading: Scale Mail
content: Scale mail is made up of dozens of small overlapping metal plates. The suit includes gauntlets.

heading: Shield, Heavy; Wooden
content: You strap a shield to your forearm and grip it with your hand. A heavy shield is so heavy that you can't use your shield hand for anything else.

heading: Shield, Heavy; Steel
content: You strap a shield to your forearm and grip it with your hand. A heavy shield is so heavy that you can't use your shield hand for anything else.

heading: Shield, Light; Wooden
content: You strap a shield to your forearm and grip it with your hand. A light shield's weight lets you carry other items in that hand, although you cannot use weapons with it.

heading: Shield, Light; Steel
content: You strap a shield to your forearm and grip it with your hand. A light shield's weight lets you carry other items in that hand, although you cannot use weapons with it.

heading: Shield Spikes

heading: Splint Mail
content: Splint mail is made up of metal strips, like banded mail. The suit includes gauntlets.

heading: Studded Leather
content: Similar to leather armor, this suit is reinforced with small metal studs.

heading: Artisan's Outfit
content: This outfit includes a shirt with buttons, a skirt or pants with a drawstring, shoes, and perhaps a cap or hat. It may also include a belt or a leather or cloth apron for carrying tools.

heading: Cleric's Vestments
content: These clothes are for performing priestly functions, not for adventuring. Cleric's vestments typically include a cassock, stole, and surplice.

heading: Cold-Weather Outfit
content: This outfit includes a wool coat, linen shirt, wool cap, heavy cloak, thick pants or skirt, and boots. This outfit grants a +5 circumstance bonus on Fortitude saving throws against exposure to cold we

heading: Courtier's Outfit
content: This outfit includes fancy, tailored clothes in whatever fashion happens to be the current style in the courts of the nobles. Anyone trying to influence nobles or courtiers while wearing street dress

heading: Entertainer's Outfit
content: This set of flashy--perhaps even gaudy--clothes is for entertaining. While the outfit looks whimsical, its practical design lets you tumble, dance, walk a tightrope, or just run (if the audience turns

heading: Explorer's Outfit
content: This set of clothes is for someone who never knows what to expect. It includes sturdy boots, leather breeches or a skirt, a belt, a shirt (perhaps with a vest or jacket), gloves, and a cloak. Rather t

heading: Monk's Outfit
content: This simple outfit includes sandals, loose breeches, and a loose shirt, and is bound together with sashes. The outfit is designed to give you maximum mobility, and it's made of high-quality fabric. Yo

heading: Noble's Outfit
content: These clothes are designed specifically to be expensive and gaudy. Precious metals and gems are worked into the clothing. A would-be noble also needs a signet ring and jewelry (worth at least 100 gp)

heading: Peasant's Outfit
content: This set of clothes consists of a loose shirt and baggy breeches, or a loose shirt and skirt or overdress. Cloth wrappings are used for shoes.

heading: Royal Outfit
content: This is just the clothing, not the royal scepter, crown, ring, and other accoutrements. Royal clothes are ostentatious, with gems, gold, silk, and fur in abundance.

heading: Scholar's Outfit
content: Perfect for a scholar, this outfit includes a robe, a belt, a cap, soft shoes, and possibly a cloak.

heading: Traveler's Outfit
content: This set of clothes consists of boots, a wool skirt or breeches, a sturdy belt, a shirt (perhaps with a vest or jacket), and an ample cloak with a hood.

heading: Inn
content: Poor accommodations at an inn amount to a place on the floor near the hearth. Common accommodations consist of a place on a raised, heated floor and the use of a blanket and a pillow. Good accommodati

heading: Meals
content: Poor meals might be composed of bread, baked turnips, onions, and water. Common meals might consist of bread, chicken stew, carrots, and watered-down ale or wine. Good meals might be composed of bread

heading: Barding, Medium Creature and Large Creature
content: Barding is a type of armor that covers the head, neck, chest, body, and possibly legs of a horse or other mount. Barding made of medium or heavy armor provides better protection than light barding, bu

heading: Bit and Bridle

heading: Dog, Guard

heading: Dog, Riding
content: This Medium dog is specially trained to carry a Small humanoid rider. It is brave in combat like a combat-trained horse. Due to its smaller stature, you take no damage when you fall from a riding dog.

content: Donkeys and mules are stolid in the face of danger, hardy, surefooted, and capable of carrying heavy loads over vast distances. Unlike a horse, a donkey or a mule is willing (though not eager) to ente

heading: Feed
content: Horses, donkeys, mules, and ponies can graze to sustain themselves, but providing feed for them is better. If you have a riding dog, you have to feed it meat.

heading: Horse
content:
A horse is suitable as a mount for a human, dwarf, elf, half-elf, or half-orc. A pony is smaller than a horse and is a suitable mount for a gnome or halfling.

A war-trained horse can be ridden into c
